short: The longest-serving heir in British history, king at seventy-three.
full:
Charles became king on his mother's death in September 2022, having been heir apparent since 1952 and Prince of Wales since 1958. As heir he used the position more actively than his predecessors, campaigning on architecture, organic farming and climate change, and founding the Prince's Trust in 1976.

His accession was managed under long-rehearsed plans, and he was crowned at Westminster Abbey on 6 May 2023 in a shortened service that included representatives of other faiths. He inherited fourteen realms beyond the United Kingdom and a Commonwealth of 56 states, with republican debate live in several of them. He has signalled a smaller working royal family and has accepted more scrutiny of the royal finances. A cancer diagnosis announced in February 2024 curtailed his public duties for much of that year, at the same time as the illness of the Princess of Wales.
